page.overview:
Who is Teclis?

Teclis, High Loremaster of Hoeth, Warden of the White Tower, and known in the Old World as Teclis of Ulthuan, is a High Elf Prince, High Elf Archmage and Loremaster of Hoeth who is considered by many to be one of the greatest and most powerful wizards the mortal world has ever known. Teclis is the twin brother of Tyrion, the famed High Elf Prince, warrior and the widely-proclaimed "Defender of Ulthuan." Being of the Line of Aenarion, each of his descendants is destined for greatness amongst the Ten Kingdoms. This has made Tyrion a masterful warrior and general, and in turn, this greatness makes Teclis proficient and knowledgeable in all arts and forms of magic.

It is said that Teclis is not a far cry to the most ancient and revered Elven archmage in history; the legendary Caledor Dragontamer, whose heroic sacrifice led to the creation of the Great Vortex which sucked the corrupting influence of Chaos from the mortal world, saving it from eternal damnation. Few within the world can match Teclis and his control over magic. No one, not even the mighty Malekith, Witch King of Naggaroth, could best him in a magical duel.

Indeed, ever since they faced one another at the Battle of Finuval Plain during the Great War Against Chaos in 2302 IC, Teclis has cemented his place in history as Malekith's only true superior in the magical arts. It is even claimed that Teclis' power approaches that of the Great Necromancer, the Liche Nagash himself, and so it is fortunate that the Loremaster has devoted his life to thwarting all malevolent powers.

The twins differ greatly in their outlook on the world. Where Tyrion sees the protection of Ulthuan as his chief duty, Teclis seeks to safeguard the whole world and those mortals of all races that live in it. Such is his ideology that he came to the aid of the Imperial general and future emperor Magnus the Pious and the forces of the Men of the Old World in the Great War Against Chaos, and with him founded the Colleges of Magic in the Empire, teaching the wizards of Men how they could safely control the Winds of Magic, even if they could never match the true mastery of the Elves.

Also known as: Teclis the Archmage.
